import pandas as pd, numpy as np, statsmodels.api as sm

class LegacyModel:
    def __init__(self):
        self._woe_tabs = {}
        self._model = None
        self._coef_series = None
        self._train_rows = None
        self._vars = ["checking","duration","history","purpose","amount","savings","employment","instalment"]

    def _bin_duration(self, x):
        bins = [-np.inf,12,24,36,np.inf]
        labels = ["lt12","12-24","24-36","36+"]
        return pd.cut(x, bins=bins, right=False, labels=labels).astype(str)

    def _bin_amount(self, x):
        x = x.copy()
        x = x.fillna(0)
        bins = [-np.inf,1400,4000,8000,np.inf]
        labels = ["lt1400","1400-4000","4000-8000","8000+"]
        return pd.cut(x, bins=bins, right=False, labels=labels).astype(str)

    def _make_bins(self, df):
        b = pd.DataFrame({
            "checking": df["status.of.existing.checking.account"].astype(str).fillna("NA"),
            "duration": self._bin_duration(df["duration.in.month"]),
            "history": df["credit.history"].astype(str).fillna("NA"),
            "purpose": df["purpose"].astype(str).fillna("NA"),
            "amount": self._bin_amount(df["credit.amount"]),
            "savings": df["savings.account.and.bonds"].astype(str).fillna("NA"),
            "employment": df["present.employment.since"].astype(str).fillna("NA"),
            "instalment": df["installment.rate.in.percentage.of.disposable.income"].astype(str).fillna("NA")
        })
        return b

    def _compute_woe(self, bins, bad):
        G = (bad == 0).sum()
        B = (bad == 1).sum()
        self._woe_tabs = {}
        for v in self._vars:
            lv = sorted(bins[v].unique())
            ng = bins[v].map(lambda l: ((bins[v] == l) & (bad == 0)).sum())
            nb = bins[v].map(lambda l: ((bins[v] == l) & (bad == 1)).sum())
            # compute per level
            woe_dict = {}
            for level in lv:
                ng_l = ((bins[v] == level) & (bad == 0)).sum()
                nb_l = ((bins[v] == level) & (bad == 1)).sum()
                w = np.log(((nb_l + 0.5) / B) / ((ng_l + 0.5) / G))
                woe_dict[level] = w
            self._woe_tabs[v] = woe_dict

    def _apply_woe(self, bins):
        out = pd.DataFrame(index=bins.index)
        for v in self._vars:
            out[f"woe_{v}"] = bins[v].map(self._woe_tabs[v])
        return out

    def fit(self, frame: pd.DataFrame, train_rows: np.ndarray | None = None) -> "LegacyModel":
        # select training rows
        if train_rows is not None:
            # train_rows are 1‑based .row values
            train_mask = frame[".row"].isin(train_rows)
            train_df = frame[train_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
        else:
            train_df = frame.copy().reset_index(drop=True)
        # target
        bad = (train_df["creditability"] == "bad").astype(int)
        # binning
        bins = self._make_bins(train_df)
        # compute WoE tables
        self._compute_woe(bins, bad)
        # apply WoE to training data
        X = self._apply_woe(bins)
        X = sm.add_constant(X, has_constant='add')
        # fit GLM
        glm = sm.GLM(bad, X, family=sm.families.Binomial())
        self._model = glm.fit(maxiter=100, tol=1e-12)
        self._coef_series = pd.Series(self._model.params)
        self._train_rows = train_rows
        return self

    def score(self, frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        if self._model is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Model has not been fitted.")
        bins = self._make_bins(frame)
        Xs = self._apply_woe(bins)
        Xs = sm.add_constant(Xs, has_constant='add')
        pd_vals = self._model.predict(Xs)
        decision = np.where(pd_vals > 0.35, "DECLINE", "APPROVE")
        out = pd.DataFrame({"score": pd_vals, "decision": decision}, index=frame.index)
        return out

    @property
    def coef(self) -> pd.Series | None:
        return self._coef_series

Implemented exact binning edges and right‑exclusive intervals as in the R script.
Missing credit.amount values are set to 0 before binning, matching R's `x[is.na(x)] <- 0`.
WoE calculation adds 0.5 to both bad and good counts before taking the log, identical to R implementation.
Decision threshold uses 0.35 (the actual code) despite a comment mentioning 0.25.
